qa_pairs.input: How do I perform a Bodyweight Squat?
qa_pairs.output: The Bodyweight Squat is a beginner-level exercise that targets Abs, Butt/Hips, Legs – Calves and Shins, Legs – Thighs. It requires No Equipment. To perform it: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width apart, toes turned slightly outward. Arms hang by your sides with palms facing inward. Retract and depress the scapulae, pulling shoulders down and back. Tighten core and abdominal muscles in a bracing pattern to stabilize the spine. Hold your chest up and out, tilt your head slightly up while shifting weight back into the heels and pushing hips rearward. Initiate by shifting hips backward and then downward, creating a simultaneous hinge at the hips and knees. As hips lower, knees travel forward slowly, but try to control the amount of forward translation of the tibia. Lower until thighs reach parallel with the floor. Keeping back, chest, and head elevated, exhale and drive the feet into the floor through the heels to extend the hips and knees. The hips and torso need to rise together while keeping heels flat and knees aligned over the second toe.

qa_pairs.input: How do I perform a Front Raise?
qa_pairs.output: The Front Raise is a beginner-level exercise that targets Shoulders. It requires Dumbbells. To perform it: Stand with dumbbells in front of your thighs using a closed, pronated grip (thumbs around the handles and palms facing your thighs). The dumbbells should rest lightly against the front of your thighs with elbows extended or holding a slight bend. You can adopt a split-stance for stability or place your feet slightly wider than hip-width. Tighten your trunk by activating your core muscles. Depress and retract your scapulae (pull your shoulders down and back), holding this throughout. Exhale as you slowly lift the dumbbells forward. Your elbows and upper arms should rise together, staying slightly ahead of your forearms and dumbbells. Once your arms pass the 60-70 degree mark (approaching shoulder height), gently rotate them upward so the inside edge of the dumbbells points slightly up. Continue until your arms are shoulder-level and roughly parallel to the floor. Maintain an upright torso with no low-back arching and keep wrists in a neutral position. Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down, keeping elbows slightly extended.
